title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
description:
Implement single-head **scaled dot-product attention**.

`Q` is a list of `m` query vectors, `K` a list of `n` key vectors (same dimension `d` as the queries) and `V` a list of `n` value vectors (any dimension). Compute

`Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V`

where softmax is applied to each row of the `m x n` score matrix. If `causal` is true, position `i` may only attend to keys `j <= i`: set the score of every `j > i` to `-inf` before the softmax so those weights become exactly 0. Return the `m` output rows.

examples.explanation: Query 0 may only see key 0, so its output is exactly V[0]. Query 1 sees both keys as before.
A zero query scores every key equally, so the output is the plain average of the values.

constraints: When causal is true, m == n.
hints: Compute one row of scores at a time: dot(q, k_j) / sqrt(d) for every key j; you never need the full matrix in memory.
Apply a numerically stable softmax to the row (subtract the row max). With -inf entries, exp(-inf - max) is 0.0 in Python, so masked keys fall out naturally.
The output row is the weighted sum of value vectors: sum_j w_j * V[j].
signature: def attention(self, Q: List[List[float]], K: List[List[float]], V: List[List[float]], causal: bool) -> List[List[float]]:
approach:
**Attention is a soft dictionary lookup: each query compares itself with every key, turns the similarities into a probability distribution, and returns the matching average of the values.** The `1 / sqrt(d)` scale keeps the dot products at unit variance when the components are; without it, large `d` pushes the softmax into saturation where gradients vanish. Masking with `-inf` rather than a large negative number guarantees weights that are exactly zero and plays well with the max-subtraction trick, because `exp(-inf) = 0.0`.

Implementation points: process one query row at a time (O(n) memory per row), reuse the stable softmax, and skip zero-weight values in the weighted sum. The causal mask requires at least one unmasked key per row (`j = i`), so the row max is always finite.

**Interview follow-ups:** How does multi-head attention differ? (split `d_model` into `h` heads, run this per head on projected Q/K/V, concatenate, project again). What are the time and memory costs for sequence length n? (O(n^2 d) time and O(n^2) score memory, the motivation for FlashAttention's tiling and online softmax). What is the KV cache in autoregressive decoding and why does it make generation O(n) per token? How would you add padding masks or relative position information?
